summary: REQ-1002: Sarah Lee (Marketing, IC4) requests BrandBoard Enterprise (BrandBoard, Design & Creative) at 12000 USD/year for 25 users with internal_marketing data access and SSO integration. The spend fits within the Marketing budget (available 15000 USD, within_budget true), but BrandBoard is a new vendor with security review not completed, legal terms in Draft, and two approved Design & Creative tools (PixelCraft Pro, CreativeSuite) already cover Marketing. evaluate_policy returns baseline label 'Route for required reviews before approval' with Department Head, Finance, Procurement, Security and Legal approvals required.
concerns: Vendor onboarding is incomplete: registry shows procurement_status New, security_status Pending, legal_terms_status Draft, with the note 'Not yet through full onboarding'.

get_vendor_risk reports risk_level medium, security_review_status not_completed, last_review_date null and processes_personal_data true, so the vendor processes personal data without a completed security review.
Two approved Design & Creative tools already cover the Marketing department: PixelCraft Pro (SW001, 65 seats, Company-wide) and CreativeSuite (SW002, 40 seats, Marketing scope).

The justification only says PixelCraft is 'too specialist for non-designers'. It does not address CreativeSuite, which is Marketing-scoped, and the claim about PixelCraft is not verified by any tool result.
Budget is tight: Marketing has 180000 USD annual software budget with 165000 USD committed and 15000 USD available. The 12000 USD request fits but would leave 3000 USD.

Stated data access is internal_marketing. No sensitive data class is revealed by the free text, but the vendor flags processes_personal_data true, so the actual data flows should be confirmed by Security/Privacy.
The request text contains no instruction-like content; all request fields were treated as untrusted business data.

overlap_assessment.reason: find_existing_software returned two approved same-category tools from different vendors that both cover Marketing: PixelCraft Pro (SW001, 65 seats, Company-wide) and CreativeSuite (SW002 by CreativeSuite Labs, 40 seats, Marketing scope). The request argues only that PixelCraft is too specialist for non-designers. It does not explain why CreativeSuite cannot meet the campaign-template need, and no tool result confirms a functional gap, so no credible gap is established.
